# Tag

Figma: [04a. Tag](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-911) · Family: 04 Data Display · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-26

Small pill-shaped indicators for displaying status, category, classification, or any short metadata. The Tag family covers three components: the main Tag (static display), Tag Removable (filter chip with X close icon), and Tag Group (container for multiple tags with inline / wrap / overflow layouts). Six tone variants (neutral / info / success / warning / error / brand) communicate semantic meaning. Used everywhere on Safqah - deal status, investor classification, sector, compliance state, risk level, and any short metadata that benefits from visual color coding.

### Tag

Small static pill that labels a category or short metadata with one of six semantic tones (sector, investor classification, document type, risk level). It is display-only and never interactive.

Level: atom · Part of: Tag Group, CardDeal

Use when:
- Sector or asset-class label on a CardDeal, such as عقاري
- Investor classification or document type in a list row or Table / Cell
- Risk level or short metadata next to a deal title
- Up to one Style=filled primary tag plus subtle secondary tags on a card

Don't use when:
- A deal or issuance lifecycle status (Raising, Funded, Late, Defaulted): use IssuanceStatusBadge (Investor)
- An attribute label such as Verified, KYC complete or Sharia-certified with an optional icon: use StatusPill
- A filter or selection the user can remove: use Tag Removable
- A deal tier or marketing ribbon (Premium, Basic, Closed): use dealTags
- Anything tappable that navigates: use Button or Link

Accessibility: Meaning must live in the Label text, never in tone color alone (WCAG 1.4.1); read as plain text, no role=button.

### Tag Removable

Tag with a built-in close X for dismissible filter chips and applied selections, for example an applied sector filter above the deals list. Always subtle style so the X stays visible.

Level: molecule · Contains: Tag · Part of: Tag Group

Use when:
- Applied filters in a deals search or filter header (Sector: عقاري)
- Chosen values in a multi-select field shown as chips
- User-picked interests or segments that can be cleared one by one

Don't use when:
- A static label the user cannot remove: use Tag
- A status or attribute label: use StatusPill
- Selecting a Saudi region chip in a selector: use RegionChip inside ProvinceSelector
- A toggle between options: use SegmentedControl_2 (or _3/_4/_5)

Accessibility: The X is a button with an accessible name like "Remove عقاري filter"; make the whole tag the 24px minimum target at Size=sm.

### Tag Group

Layout container that arranges two or more Tags inline, wrapped, or as the first three plus a +N overflow counter. Spacing between tags is fixed by the component.

Level: molecule · Contains: Tag, Tag Removable · Part of: CardDeal

Use when:
- Two or more tags together on a deal card (sector + type + risk), Layout=inline
- A variable number of applied filters, Layout=wrap
- Dense rows or table cells with many categories, Layout=overflow showing +N

Don't use when:
- A single label: use Tag on its own
- Lifecycle status next to categories: place one IssuanceStatusBadge (Investor) separately, do not group it as a Tag
- Wrap layout inside a horizontally scrolling Table / Cell: use Layout=overflow

Accessibility: Expose as a list of labels; the +N counter needs an accessible name like "4 more tags" and Western digits.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Tag is one of the most-used components on Safqah. Deal cards show status (Open / Funded / Closed), investor records show classification (Accredited / Retail / Institutional), transaction tables show state (Pending / Completed / Failed), and document lists show type (PDF / Image / Spreadsheet) - all using the Tag component with its six semantic tones.

Three components in the family cover the spectrum: the main Tag for static display (the vast majority of use cases), Tag Removable when users need to dismiss filter chips, and Tag Group as a container layout for showing multiple tags together. Pick the smallest component that fits the need - Tag for one indicator, Tag Group for a collection.

### At a glance

### Atomic architecture

Three components covering display, interaction, and grouping. Same visual language; different intent.

Display - Tag · 72 variants

Static status/category indicator. Variants: 6 tones × 3 sizes × 2 styles × 2 directions. The default workhorse - use for ~90% of tag use cases. Style "subtle" is the default low-prominence appearance; style "filled" reserves higher prominence for emphasis.

Interactive - Tag Removable · 36 variants

Tag with X close icon. Variants: 6 tones × 3 sizes × 2 directions. Always subtle style. Use specifically for filter chips, applied selections, multi-select chip groups - anywhere the user can dismiss the tag. The X is a button affordance, not a decorative element.

Container - Tag Group · 6 variants

Layout primitive for multiple tags. Variants: 3 layouts × 2 directions. Layouts: inline (single row, horizontal scroll), wrap (multiple rows, auto-flow), overflow (3 tags + "+N more" indicator for compact contexts). Spacing/8 between tags. Use whenever you need 2+ tags together.

### Tones - six semantic colors

Six tones communicate meaning. Pick the tone that matches the semantic intent - never use a tone for purely decorative color. Users learn the meaning of each tone over time, so consistent tone-to-meaning mapping builds reliable visual language across the app.

Neutral

Default gray. Use for category labels with no semantic meaning - sectors ("Real Estate", "Healthcare"), document types ("PDF", "Image"), generic classification. The most common tone, low visual weight.

Info

Blue. Use for informational signals that aren't alerts - "New", "Updated", "Pinned", "Draft", new feature labels. Catches attention without urgency.

Success

Green. Use for positive completed states - "Funded", "Approved", "Active", "Paid", "Verified". Signals a positive outcome that doesn't need user action.

Warning

Amber/orange. Use for attention states that aren't errors - "Closing soon", "Pending review", "Action needed", "Awaiting approval". Signals "look at this" without panic.

Error

Red. Use for negative/blocked states - "Overdue", "Failed", "Rejected", "Expired", "Cancelled". Reserve for genuine problems the user needs to address.

Brand

Safqah primary green. Use sparingly for featured/highlighted content - "Featured", "Recommended", "Top deal", "Editor's pick". Reserve for ~5% of tags; overuse dilutes meaning.

### Styles - filled vs subtle

Two style choices control visual weight. Style "subtle" is the default and the most common choice; "filled" is reserved for higher prominence - usually when you want a tag to compete with other visual elements.

Subtle (default)

Light tinted background + darker text in the same tone. Lower visual weight, integrates calmly with surrounding content. Use for ~90% of tag instances.

Filled

Solid tone background + white text. Higher visual weight, demands attention. Use sparingly - for the single most important tag in a context (e.g., the primary deal status badge on a deal card).

> **Tip:** Don't use filled tags everywhere. A row of all-filled tags looks like a stoplight - every tag screaming for attention. Filled is for the ONE most important tag in a context. Subtle is for everything else.

### Sizes

Three sizes match the content density of the surrounding context. Padding, font, and overall height scale together.

Large (28dp, 14dp font)

Use in detail views, deal headers, card headers - anywhere the tag is a primary signal at the top of a section.

Medium (24dp, 12dp font)

The default. Use in cards, list rows, table cells, anywhere the tag is inline metadata. Most common size.

Small (20dp, 11dp font)

Use in dense tables, sidebar lists, inline next to small text - anywhere space is constrained.

### Layouts - Tag Group container

When showing multiple tags, use Tag Group with the right layout for the context. Three layouts cover the spectrum from inline to overflow.

Inline - single row

All tags on one row, horizontal scroll if needed. Use when you have a known small set (3-5 tags) and consistent ordering matters - e.g., a deal's sector + status + investor type displayed in a fixed sequence.

Wrap - multiple rows

Tags wrap to subsequent rows when the container width is exceeded. Use when the number of tags is variable and you want all of them visible - e.g., user-selected interest tags, applied filters in a search results header.

Overflow - +N more

Shows the first 3 tags + a "+N more" indicator for the rest. Tapping "+N more" expands to wrap layout (or opens a dropdown). Use in compact contexts where vertical space is limited - table rows, list items, card secondary content.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

Tag content flips for Arabic - labels right-aligned, removable X icon moves to the leading edge (left in RTL). The Tag Group also flips: in RTL, the first tag appears on the right, subsequent tags flow right-to-left.

LTR

English / default. Tag labels left-aligned. Removable X icon on the right (trailing). Tag Group: first tag on left, flow rightward. Numbers in "+N more" use Western numerals.

RTL

Arabic. Tag labels right-aligned (e.g., "تم التمويل", "قريب الإغلاق"). Removable X icon on the left (visually leading). Tag Group: first tag on right, flow leftward. Numbers in "+N more" use Arabic-Indic numerals (+٤).

### Code examples

How to consume Tag components in Flutter.

### Flutter - basic static tag

```dart
// Deal status tag on a deal card
SafqahTag(
  label: 'Funded',
  tone: TagTone.success,
  size: TagSize.md,
  style: TagStyle.subtle,
)
```

### Flutter - removable filter chip

```dart
// Applied filter chip in a search results header
SafqahTagRemovable(
  label: 'Real Estate',
  tone: TagTone.neutral,
  size: TagSize.md,
  onRemove: () {
    setState(() {
      _appliedFilters.remove('Real Estate');
    });
  },
  // aria-label automatically generated as "Remove Real Estate filter"
)
```

### Flutter - Tag Group with overflow

```dart
// Compact tag group on a deal card showing categories
SafqahTagGroup(
  layout: TagGroupLayout.overflow,
  maxVisible: 3,
  tags: dealCategories.map((cat) => SafqahTag(
    label: cat.name,
    tone: TagTone.neutral,
    size: TagSize.sm,
  )).toList(),
  onOverflowTap: () {
    // Show all tags in a bottom sheet or expanded view
    _showAllCategories(context);
  },
)
```

### Flutter - Arabic RTL with multiple tones

```dart
// Arabic deal card with status + sector + risk tags
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: SafqahTagGroup(
    layout: TagGroupLayout.inline,
    tags: [
      SafqahTag(
        label: 'تم التمويل',  // Funded
        tone: TagTone.success,
        style: TagStyle.filled,  // Primary status - full prominence
      ),
      SafqahTag(
        label: 'عقاري',  // Real Estate
        tone: TagTone.neutral,
      ),
      SafqahTag(
        label: 'مخاطر منخفضة',  // Low risk
        tone: TagTone.info,
      ),
    ],
  ),
)
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · Deal status on a deal card: Use the success tone with subtle style for "Funded". Subtle works in cards because the deal title is the primary focus. One tag per status. If you need a "primary" tag plus secondary categories, use filled for the primary status only.
- **Don't** · Deal status on a deal card: Don't use filled success tag for every funded deal - when you have a list of 20 deals all marked "Funded" with filled green tags, the page becomes visually loud. Don't use multiple filled tags on the same card - they fight each other.
- **Do** · Filter chips in search results header: Use Tag Removable for applied filters that users can dismiss. Neutral tone for categorical filters (sector, type), other tones only when the filter ITSELF has semantic color (e.g., "Status: Funded" could be success-tone). X button has aria-label="Remove [filter] filter".
- **Don't** · Filter chips in search results header: Don't use static Tag for filters - users will tap expecting it to be dismissible. Don't use a separate "X" button next to a static tag - Tag Removable bakes the X into the tag for a single touch target. Don't use color to indicate "active filter" - the presence in the filter bar already shows it's active.
- **Do** · Arabic RTL deal with status tags: Use the RTL direction variant. Tag labels right-aligned with Arabic text ("تم التمويل", "قريب الإغلاق"). When in a Tag Group, the first tag appears on the right (visually leading), subsequent tags flow leftward. X icons (if removable) move to the left edge.
- **Don't** · Arabic RTL deal with status tags: Don't use LTR direction in Arabic contexts - the tag content alignment will be wrong even if the text itself is Arabic. Don't hardcode English status labels ("Funded") in Arabic UI - use the localized strings ("تم التمويل"). Don't mix LTR and RTL tags in the same group.
- **Do** · Status hierarchy in a deal listing: Use Tag Group with inline layout for a fixed small set of status tags (3-5). For one primary status, use filled style; for secondary categories (sector, type), use subtle style. Visual hierarchy emerges from style contrast - the filled tag draws the eye first.
- **Don't** · Status hierarchy in a deal listing: Don't mix unlimited tags without bounding - use the overflow layout when you might have 10+ items. Don't use wrap layout in a horizontally scrolling table cell - the wrap will break the row alignment. Don't use all-filled tags in a group - pick one filled tag at most.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** Tag is the first component in the 04 family (display/feedback). It's a foundational primitive - every dashboard, listing, table, and card view will use it. Treat tone-to-meaning consistency seriously: if "Pending" is warning in one place and info in another, users learn the wrong mental model.

> **Info:** Six tones is more than most design systems (Material has 4, Carbon has 5). The brand tone is the differentiator - it's reserved for Safqah-specific featured content. Don't use the brand tone for generic positive states (success handles that); reserve it for editorial emphasis like "Featured deal", "Top pick".

> **Info:** Subtle vs filled is a visual weight decision, not a semantic one. Both styles communicate the same meaning (a success tag means success regardless of style). The choice is about how loud the tag should be relative to its surroundings. Default to subtle.

> **Warning:** Radius/Full token name (with capital F) is the correct variable - there's also a lowercase radius/full but the design system uses the capitalized version. Worth noting because the variable picker shows both and they have different values (Radius/Full = 9999, radius/full might be different).

> **Warning:** TEXT property defaultValue gotcha hit again (locked constraint #11). Tag labels per tone needed direct text setting on each variant since the property defaultValue takes from the first variant only. Workaround: removed componentPropertyReferences.characters on non-default variants and set characters directly.

> **Info:** Tag Group "overflow" layout shows "+N" with a hardcoded count of 4 in Figma. In runtime code, the count is dynamic based on actual tag overflow. The "+٤" in the RTL variant uses Arabic-Indic numerals as a convention - runtime framework switches numeral system based on locale.

> **Warning:** Removable tags are always subtle style - never filled. Reason: the X close icon needs to be visible against the tag background. On filled tones with white text, the white X disappears into the colored background; subtle tones with tone-color X provide proper contrast. If you NEED a filled removable tag, the X color would need to be inverse - design carefully.

> **Info:** The "+N more" indicator in Tag Group overflow is intentionally NOT a Tag instance - it's a custom pill with bg/disabled background and text/muted text. This signals "this isn't a category, it's a count indicator" through visual differentiation. If you make it a real Tag, users will try to dismiss it.

> **Warning:** Color-blind users - the green/red distinction (success/error) is the most affected by color blindness. ALWAYS pair tag tones with meaningful text labels - "Funded" + green, "Failed" + red. The label is the accessible semantic; color is reinforcement only. This is why the Tag has no icon-only variant.

> **Warning:** WCAG considerations - touch target for Tag Removable X close button needs to be ≥ 24dp tall (WCAG 2.5.5 AA). The sm size X icon is 10dp, so the entire tag should become the tap target on sm with the X as a visual indicator. Wrap the tag in a Pressable for proper touch target on sm.

> **Warning:** Don't use Tag for navigation. Tags are status indicators, not buttons. If you need a "Filter by Real Estate" affordance that navigates, build a separate Chip Button component or use the standard Button component with smaller size. Tag is for display + dismiss, not for navigation.

> **Warning:** FONT WORKAROUND - Same as the rest of the components. All text uses IBM Plex Sans Medium for the label. Font/Size, Font/Line-Height, and Font/Weight all bound to variables on every text node.
